newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 14.

text.p: Rite Aid Corp has agreed to buy Thrifty Payless TFYP.OB Holdings for $1.4 billion in stock plus the assumption of about $890 million in debt, the Wall Street Journal reported Monday.
- Archer Daniels Midland Co might plead guilty on Monday to criminal charges and pay $100 million in fines following a federal investigation into price fixing in the sale of agricultural products.
- USAir Group Inc is thinking about ordering up to 120 jetliners from either Boeing Co, Airbus Industrie, and McDonnell Douglas Corp in a $5 billion deal.
- The Canadian Automobile Workers union's strike against General Motors Corp is about to force the company to close U.S. assembly operations.
- U.S. producer prices edged 0.2 percent higher in September and the month's retail sales rose 0.7 percent.
- WMX Technologies Inc is considering selling its interest in ServiceMaster and Wessex Water and raise $1 billion.
- U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation and Securities and Exchange Commission are investigating government and financial corruption in South Florida.
- Last week's FBI sting that arrested 46 people showed how manipulating small stock prices has become a huge problem.
- The NASD accused Stratton Oakmont and four of its officials of defrauding investors during five initial public offerings.
- New York City's mayor's struggle with Time Warner Inc over Fox news channel of News Corp Ltd is viewed as a test of his power to determine what the city will watch.
- Motorola Inc is planning a $6.1 billion network of 72 satellites capable of global voice, video, and data links.
- The United States convinced Mexican tomato farmers to set a floor under the prices of the produce when they ship them to the U.S. market.
- U.S. Energy Secretary O'Leary called on oil executives to try to avoid a heating oil crisis this winter.
- Traders and market analysts are wondering whether Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp has grown too big after having acquired hundreds of competitors in recent years.
